A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Neural Graduated Assignment for MCES. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite reformatting and relocation of content.

before.justification: V2 reports original MCES, graph similarity, retrieval, ablation, and QAP results in Section 6 and Appendices F–G.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds unlabeled MCES results, baseline comparisons, and temperature trajectories during training.

M1.justification: Appendix G.6 introduces the evaluated NGA-GPS variant, replacing the GCN backbone with a Graph Transformer using random-walk structural encodings and attention. The main NGA objective, ACG construction, assignment refinement, and Gumbel/Hungarian procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V3 adds one structure-only MCES scenario, AIDS-unlabeled, by replacing all atom labels with carbon and all bonds with single bonds (G.6). The existing labeled molecular datasets, similarity and retrieval tasks, synthetic QAP benchmarks, and QAPLIB coverage are retained.

E2.justification: GANN-GM is newly evaluated in the molecular MCES comparison in Table 1. Gurobi is also added to the Figure 8 runtime case studies, although it already appeared in v2's main comparison. Other retained experiments preserve their comparator sets.

E3.justification: The added unlabeled experiment introduces label-collapsing preprocessing and a GCN/GPS comparison using eight layers and 32 hidden dimensions, with four attention heads for GPS. New Figure 12 tracks temperatures through 300 epochs. Existing splits, 60-second instance budgets, and 200-epoch supervised training settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix G.6 tests robustness to absent labels and the benefit of structural encodings. New Figure 12 examines temperature evolution during training, extending the existing near-convergence analysis. Earlier component ablations, parameter sensitivities, and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions already display means and one-standard-deviation bands for temperature distributions and loss curves. V3 adds no seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or statistical testing procedures. The loss plot's renumbering from Figure 12 to Figure 13 preserves its uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds GANN-GM accuracies of 49.76, 72.18, and 63.47, while existing entries remain unchanged. New Table 9 reports 93.72 for NGA and 94.37 for NGA-GPS on AIDS-unlabeled. Gurobi runtime curves and training-temperature trajectories are also added; existing Tables 2–8 retain their values.

T1.justification: V2's Appendix C.3 discusses O(M) ACG operations; v3's C.2 adds O(E^2) construction-time and O(M) storage reasoning, including a new sparsity inequality. Mathematical definitions, Theorem 1, both propositions, and the proofs in Appendices B, D, and E are otherwise unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-data-free MCES approximation, learnable temperatures, convergence and exploration, scalability, interpretability, and downstream applications. The additional experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: V3 adds implicit-bias interpretations of factorization (D.2), clarifies the local scope of Theorem 1 (G.3), and discusses pairwise limitations, multi-graph extensions, and label-noise alternatives (H–I). These extend existing explanations. The earlier statement that unlabeled graphs remain unaddressed is nevertheless retained despite G.6.

D1.justification: V3 adds a reported public code location and README-based reproduction guidance, plus unlabeled-data preparation, GPS configuration, and sparse-storage details. Existing hardware, optimization settings, and core hyperparameters move from v2's Appendix C.2 to Section 6.2 without substantive changes. Repository functionality is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: V3 adds references concerning GANN-GM, GraphGPS, other graph-matching methods, implicit bias and factorization, and cycle-consistent multi-graph matching. Appendices D.2 and H introduce corresponding conceptual connections. The central positioning and novelty claims remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. Implementation details move into the main text, several discussions expand, and acknowledgements, ethics/reproducibility, and LLM-usage statements are added. Wording receives limited edits, and citations switch from numerical to author–year style without extensive narrative rewriting.

P2.justification: The paper is comprehensively retypeset into the ICLR template, changing title treatment, typography, margins, headers, and display sizing and placement. Figure 8 gains a comparator and revised legend/axes; Figure 12 and Table 9 are added. Existing loss and sampling plots are retained as Figures 13 and 14.

improvement.justification: The added baseline comparisons, unlabeled MCES evaluation, temperature trajectories, and code-access disclosure provide useful validation and reproducibility support for the retained contribution. The net gain is limited by an unreconciled unlabeled-graph limitation in Appendix H and C.2's unsupported inference that E^2 is much smaller than N^2 from bounded molecular degree.
